title: Multilingual rerank regression harness and latency optimizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a reproducible regression harness and staged rollout strategy for new cross-encoder reranker variants (including compact and quantized variants) across our top 10 languages, and optimise request routing and batching to meet 95th %-ile latency SLOs without regressing ranking quality. This ticket covers offline evaluation, infrastructure changes to the reranker endpoint, a canary/AB rollout plan via Console, and automated gating that blocks rollouts if key metrics degrade. We will ensure graceful fallback to the existing bi-encoder+approx pipeline and add observability for per-language NDCG/MRR and latency/cost tradeoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible offline evaluation pipeline that produces NDCG@10, MRR, and latency profiles per language for each candidate model build
Automated regression test that fails CI if NDCG@10 drops >1.5% or MRR drops >1.0% compared to baseline on the stable eval set
Endpoint changes that reduce 95th %-ile token latency for large-sequence rerank requests by at least 25% in RU (Europe) region versus current shipping configuration
Canary rollout through Console that runs 10% traffic for 48 hours with automatic rollback on metric regressions
Fallback chain implemented: if compact cross-encoder exceeds latency budget, route to bi-encoder + fast approximate rerank with documented quality delta
Dashboard with per-model, per-language panels and alerts for latency P95, token cost, NDCG@10 drop, and error rate
work_items: Define stable multilingual eval sets (holdout queries + human labels) for top 10 languages; store as CSV on GCS
Implement offline harness: containerised runner that computes NDCG@k, MRR, query latency distributions; integrate into Jenkins/CI
Benchmark candidate models (full float, FP16, int8 quantized) on representative GPU types and track mem/latency/cost
Add adaptive batching knobs to reranker endpoint: max_batch_size, latency_budget_ms, per-language queue prioritization
Implement routing policy in smart-router to prefer region-local model variants and to trigger fallback based on dynamic latency signals
Build Console canary configuration and rollout playbook; include automatic gating triggers and manual override steps
Instrument dashboards and SLO alerts in Grafana/Tempo; surface model-level regressions to #rerank-alerts channel
benchmarks_and_targets: Quality baseline: current cross-encoder baseline NDCG@10 = 0.682 (EN), MRR = 0.573
Target regression guardrails: NDCG@10 >= baseline - 0.015, MRR >= baseline - 0.01 across languages
Latency targets: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 150ms for typical 8-16 candidate rerank batches in US/EU regions
Memory targets: model working set < 22GB on p4d-style GPU for multi-model hosting with 4 concurrent workers
Cost guidance: quantized variant should reduce per-request GPU cost by >= 30% vs FP16 while meeting quality targets
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (offline): evaluate 4 candidate variants on holdout sets and select top 2 by quality+cost proxy
Phase 1 (staging): deploy models to staging cluster, run synthetic traffic and end-to-end latency/trace validation
Phase 2 (canary): route 5-10% production traffic for 48-72h, compare per-language NDCG and P95 latency; block if thresholds breach
Phase 3 (regional ramp): increment traffic to 50% in a single region, validate cost/behavior, then global ramp to 100% with gradual roll steps
Auto-rollback: CI/CD rule to rollback if model NDCG drop > threshold or P95 latency increases > 40% sustained for 30m
monitoring_and_alerts: Grafana: per-model per-language NDCG@10 and MRR time series (1h/6h/24h windows)
Grafana: latency histograms, P50/P95/P99, and token-level cost burn charts
Alert rules: NDCG drop > 1.5% (critical), P95 latency > 200ms (critical), error rate > 0.5% (warning)
Pager duty playbook: who to page for quality regressions vs infra regressions
implementation_notes: Prefer int8 dynamic quantization for compact variants; evaluate post-training quantization and awareness of per-layer outliers
When evaluating latency, include router + network + model time; synthetic single-region intra-VPC tests and multi-region over-the-wire tests
KV/prefix caching optimization: pin frequently-seen prefixes in LRU cache with eviction tie-breaker by query frequency to reduce recompute
Ensure model artifacts are versioned and signed; include model metadata with tokenization details, expected max_seq_len, and supported languages
open_risks: Quality regressions in low-resource languages where holdout sets are small; may require more human labeling budget
False positives from automated gating when traffic distribution changes (e.g., seasonal language mix) — need rolling baselines
GPU memory fragmentation could limit co-hosting multiple variants; may require dedicated pools for heavy models
Quantization edge-cases producing occasional severe misrank for specific query constructs
next_steps: Lock holdout dataset and begin initial offline runs using current top-3 candidate models (owner: Liang Wu)
Merge CI job that runs regression harness on every model PR and posts pass/fail to GitHub PR (owner: Connor Miles)
Create Console canary config and runbook draft for SRE review (owner: Maya Thompson)
Schedule cross-team review with PM and Design to validate rollout UX and customer comms (owner: Aisha Patel)
